maria: Heads-up — customer acme-789 says their usage CSV export for 2025-02-10 and 2025-02-11 is empty, but the invoice shows ~1.2M tokens for those dates. They sent the CSV and a screenshot of the invoice.

maria: CSV snippet:
```
date,account_id,tokens
2025-02-09,acme-789,41234
2025-02-10,acme-789,
2025-02-11,acme-789,
2025-02-12,acme-789,5231
```

maria: API /v1/usage/daily?start=2025-02-09&end=2025-02-12 also returns no rows for 02-10/11. Can someone triage? :eyes:

ashok: @maria — can you paste the invoice id and whether this is hosted (prod) or a dedicated account? Also timezone (they're EU-based?).

maria: invoice: INV-2025-ACME-0442, hosted prod, timezone CET. I attached the customer's note: "we only see a dip in CSV but charges still applied"

ashok: thanks. I'll check the aggregation and export jobs. Preliminary runbook: check billing_aggregates for tokens, then check export pipeline logs.

ashok: quick diagnostic: I can see aggregated tokens in billing_aggregates for those dates (rows present), which explains the invoice. The daily CSV export job that runs to S3 on 02-12 failed due to a transient worker crash and a partition marker was skipped. That caused the downstream CSV generator to treat 02-10/02-11 as empty partitions. Root cause: export-worker v2.3.1 had an off-by-one partition check when retry count > 0.

ashok: I've queued a backfill job (job id backfill-907) to regenerate the CSV partitions for 2025-02-10 and 2025-02-11 and re-run the exporter. ETA ~4 hours. Billing system not affected — invoices already reflect aggregates.

billing-bot: Backfill job created: backfill-907. ETA 4h. Notifying export-service on-call.

maria: good, can we give the customer a temporary way to pull the raw events so they can reconcile before the CSV is backfilled?

ashok: yes — workaround: use the raw usage API to pull events and sum tokens. Example: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCLOUD_KEY" \  
  "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/usage/raw?account=acme-789&start=2025-02-10&end=2025-02-11" | jq '.events[] | {date: .date, tokens: .tokens}'
```
Or run this SQL on the analytics replica: 
```sql
SELECT date, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id='acme-789' AND date BETWEEN '2025-02-10' AND '2025-02-11'
GROUP BY date;
```

sophie: I'll message the customer with the workaround and the expected ETA. If the CSV isn't fixed within 24h we should offer a manual export and a goodwill credit — ping me when it's completed. :+1:

ashok: noted. I'll follow up here when backfill finishes.

maria: thanks — I'll keep the case open and add the customer's reconciliation request.

billing-bot: Backfill job backfill-907 status: in-progress.

ashok: backfill kicked and exporter re-run started. Monitoring logs now. If anyone needs the raw token counts I can paste the summed rows here.

maria: please paste if available, customer wants immediate confirmation.

ashok: export reprocessed successfully. CSV now contains rows for 02-10 and 02-11. Closing the pipeline side of the loop. Please confirm with customer that their CSV download shows the rows.
